newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ICRC confirms Iraq to discuss prison visits.
newsitem.headline: ICRC confirms Iraq to discuss prison visits.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) confirmed on Tuesday that Iraqi authorities had agreed to discuss a plan for the humanitarian agency to visit detainees in its prisons, adding that talks would begin next week.

Rolin Wavre, ICRC spokesman, said Baghdad's offer was made last month in Geneva during a closed-door meeting of an ICRC committee trying to resolve the fate of some 600 Kuwaitis missing since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.

The detention centre visits would be the first carried out by the ICRC in Iraq, Wavre said, as the Swiss-run agency has previously been involved only in limited visits and the repatriations of prisoners from the Gulf War and the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War.
"We have never visited detainees in Iraq in a general way," he told Reuters.

In New York on Friday, Iraqi U.N. envoy Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon told reporters of the offer to allow the ICRC to "visit our prisons and camps of detention in Iraq in order to help out with the process of searching for the missing people".
Wavre told Reuters: "We confirm that we were approached by the Iraqi authorities who say they are ready to discuss an ICRC proposal to visit detainees in Iraq."
"A technical mission will go to Baghdad next week to discuss modalities of the visits," he added. No exact date has been set.
ICRC's terms for such visits include access to all detention centres, the right to make repeated visits, and the right to speak to detainees without witnesses.
Once prison visits began, they could lead to an improvement in the conditions of detention, Wavre added.

The Iraqi offer came from Riyahd Al-Qaisi, first under-secretary for foreign affairs, at a February 18 meeting of the ICRC tripartite commission which was investigating the fate of some 600 Kuwaitis and other third-party nationals missing since the Gulf War.
"Kuwait is looking for 600 people. That is another dossier being looked at in the tripartite commission," Wavre said. "That is the link but it is not the goal."
